places.name: The Held Breath
sources: module 20 §12.3b hard-to-reach types (underwater grottoes, air pockets, flooded cellars)
uesp:Lore:Argonian (amphibious physiology; the crossing is priced around held breath)

why.founding: A maintained air pocket on a flooded root route, kept so the crossing is survivable.
why.siteAdvantages: The midpoint of the longest flooded branch in the region.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; it is maintained by whoever passes. Nobody lives here; it is maintained by whoever passes, on an interior custom that a shelter you use unrepaired is a shelter you have stolen.
why.pressures: The seal leaks and the pocket is smaller each decade. The seal leaks and the pocket is smaller each decade, and the Waykeepers who could reseal it will not work outside a paid line.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing it makes the flooded route impassable. Losing it makes the flooded route impassable and pushes every crossing onto the long root gallery, which is a day and a band of danger worse.

preferences: landforms: sinkhole, cove, islet, waterfall
water relation: fully enclosed by water
neighbours: inside a drowned or flooded place

places.traversalFallback: walk the surface route (two days, D5 ground)

vibe.silhouette: none at all from outside; it is found by diving
vibe.palette: root-brown under carried light, gold beads on the underside of a limb, dark loam threaded with pale hair-roots, a red flower nobody will pick
vibe.materials: root braided into wall thickness the way a basket is braided; vine cord gone slack and tied over itself twice; sap-rubber gaskets on the dry stores; xanmeer block beside it left unquarried and untouched
vibe.signatureFeature: A dry bubble the size of a room, thirty metres down a flooded gallery, with a tally of everyone who has rested in it cut into the root.
vibe.condition: holding, but the next bad season decides it
vibe.mood: relief with a countdown attached
vibe.approach: You reach it on one breath or you do not reach it.
vibe.senses: the boards springing underfoot at every step; chimes, and a counting voice keeping time with them; no echo — the green eats it

places.name: Alten Markmont
sources: Lore:Alten Markmont (Arena gazetteer); Lore:East Empire Company

why.founding: An outsider-facing trading station built where the southern water route met the Helstrom approach; the alten- prefix marks it as never Argonian.
why.siteAdvantages: A landing on deep-enough water at the last point outsiders were tolerated.
why.occupantsMotive: A skeleton staff of two factors and whoever is sheltering in the warehouses. The two factors are paid a retainer by a company that no longer trades here, on the theory that a lapsed post is cheaper to hold than to re-license.
why.pressures: The interior tolerates it and does not need it; the trade it was built for stopped. The interior tolerates it and does not need it; the trade it was built for stopped, and the warehouses now shelter people the factors are not allowed to register.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single busy season would refill it — that is the point of keeping it standing. A single busy season would refill it — that is the point of keeping it standing, and the Helstrom assembly has quietly decided it never will be.

preferences: landforms: river-mouth, confluence, any-firm-ground
water relation: on a navigable route inland
neighbours: too far inland for its own logistics

vibe.silhouette: a company mark on a wall of a building far too large for its occupancy
vibe.palette: clear brown with the bottom visible and green above, grey silt drying in plates, the amber all in the buckets, none on the tree, red flower reflected in still water
vibe.materials: the trained root dead standing, grey and hard as bone; withy lashing re-laid every wet season; layered frond roof, sap-black along the ridges; woven grass matting, the only clean thing here
vibe.signatureFeature: Imperial warehouse frontage, never blended with a single Argonian building, standing over a quay that the marsh has taken back to the knee.
vibe.condition: left in order, which is the unsettling part
vibe.mood: commercial architecture with nobody to trade with; hollow and dry-rotting
vibe.approach: The stone shows through the reeds a long way before the buildings resolve — the only straight lines in the region.
vibe.senses: cold coming off the standing water; bone and tin chimes, tuned in fourths; wet bark and cut root, like a woodyard in rain; no birds within earshot, and that is recent

places.name: Thousand-Chimes
sources: Lore:Bright-Throat Village; Lore:Argonian (jewellery, guarded weaving secrets)

why.founding: A craft village that makes the bone and tin chimes through which half the province listens to its Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside a hero Hist whose wind is reliable — the chimes are tuned against the tree that will hang them.
why.occupantsMotive: Chime-makers whose tuning is a religious qualification, not a trade skill. Tuning is examined and licensed by the tree-minders, so a maker who loses the qualification loses the craft and the village at once.
why.pressures: Cheap cast chimes from the cities are undercutting them and, they say, mistranslating the trees. Cheap cast chimes from the cities are undercutting them and, they say, mistranslating the trees — an accusation the tree-minders have declined to rule on for six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority. A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority, and the coastal foundries that cast them would take the whole province's trade within a decade.

preferences: landforms: cliff-bench, flood-high, any-firm-ground
water relation: landing plus access to its raw material
neighbours: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

notableNpcSlots: the chime-maker
the deelith who teaches the trade

vibe.materials: living root walls with the growth points tied back each season; lashing of split cane where the withy ran out; sap-resin caulk in every seam; chimes taken down and stacked

places.name: Long-Stride

why.founding: A village that breeds the only animals that can carry a load across the interior's soft ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Wide firm grazing on a flood-high rise with a soft-ground schooling paddock beside it.
why.occupantsMotive: Breeders who supply every interior porter route and price accordingly. Breeders who supply every interior porter route and price accordingly, and who will sell a gelded steed to anyone and a breeding pair to nobody.
why.pressures: Their stock is worth stealing and the roads they supply are raided. Their stock is worth stealing and the roads they supply are raided, so a third of their yearly yield now goes to escorts rather than to buyers.
why.wouldChangeIf: A road built into the interior would end their monopoly overnight. A road built into the interior would end their monopoly overnight — which is one reason the village has never supported a road survey.

the ka-deelith who breaks them

places.name: The Staying Stone
sources: Lore:Wamasu (Haynekhtnamet of Shadowfen received offerings to stop seasonal flooding)

why.siteAdvantages: The pinch point where the flood enters this basin.

why.pressures: The floods have not obeyed for three years and the villages are blaming each other. The floods have not obeyed for three years and the villages are blaming each other, chiefly the one whose turn fell in the worst year.
why.wouldChangeIf: One more bad year and the shrine will be abandoned or rebuilt bigger. One more bad year and the shrine will be abandoned or rebuilt bigger, and either decision breaks the four-village compact that is the district's only joint institution.

preferences: landforms: oxbow, any-shallow-marsh, ravine, spring-head
water relation: facing the creature's water
neighbours: between a village and a lair

vibe.approach: A stone in the water with fresh and rotted offerings side by side.

places.name: Keeps-the-Egg
sources: Lore:Hist (a settlement without a Hist is always political)

why.occupantsMotive: Custodians of a memory nobody can currently read.
why.pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg; one has offered to buy it. Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg; one has offered to buy it, and the offer was made publicly so that refusing it would look like hoarding.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reading the Egg — which the main quest's archivists could — would resolve or destroy them. Reading the Egg — which the main quest's archivists could — would resolve or destroy them, and every claimant tribe knows which outcome it is betting on.

preferences: landforms: flood-high, any-firm-ground, oxbow

neighbours: neighbours argue about taking them in

the naheesh who will not have the clutch spoken of

vibe.palette: grey water, green banks, nothing between them, bone-white peeled root, no sap showing anywhere, which is the news, red flowers fallen and browning on the boards

vibe.mood: grief institutionalised into a job of work

places.name: The Lit Fen
sources: Lore:Wamasu (luminescent organs); Lore:Guar (Glowgill); module 55 (night is authored world state, so night-only places are legitimate)

why.founding: A fen where the water itself lights at night from Hist-flower fall.
why.siteAdvantages: Still water directly downstream of a hero Hist's grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the villages come to look, once a year. Nobody; the villages come to look, once a year, on a night fixed by the Tsoko stones rather than by the fen.
why.pressures: It only lights while the tree above flowers, which is a diagnostic nobody wants to need. It only lights while the tree above flowers, which is a diagnostic nobody wants to need — and this year the light came late and stopped early.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree failing would put the fen out. The tree failing would put the fen out, and the fen going out is how the district would learn of it, weeks before the grove admitted anything.

preferences: landforms: oxbow, any-shallow-marsh, cove, sinkhole, spring-head, islet
water relation: still or tidal water, undisturbed
neighbours: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

vibe.silhouette: the light itself, at night, from further than any daytime cue in this province works
vibe.palette: tea-black water under green shade, white sand where the channel turns, amber crusted and cracked, months old, one red flower and nothing else red for a mile, green-blue glow after dark

places.name: The Raw Hold

places.name: No-Tree Camp
sources: Lore:Lukiul; League of Open Water (quest plan); Lore:Hist

why.siteAdvantages: Ground nobody claims because no tree's roots reach it — which is exactly the point.

why.pressures: The interior tribes regard them as a category error; the League of Open Water regards them as a cause. The interior tribes regard them as a category error; the League of Open Water regards them as a cause, and its coastal money is beginning to arrive.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tree taking them in would dissolve the settlement, and some of them do not want that. A tree taking them in would dissolve the settlement, and some of them do not want that — which is the argument that splits the camp every winter.
